surface_mechanism_description: The growth of WN xCy films on SiC is similar to that on PECVD SiO2, explained by decomposition of the tri-ethylboron precursor, giving rise to a carbon rich WN xCy-oxide interface. The presence of a carbon-rich layer, resulting from TEB precursor decomposition, at the SiO2–WNxCy interface results in a SiO2 surface reacting similar to a SiC surface.
evidence: The surface composition of 2 days old ( Fig. 1a) and 2 months ( Fig. 1b) old SiC samples was measured by XPS. Two peaks can be observed at 100.1 eV and 101.8 eV corresponding to SiC and silicon oxycarbide (SiOx–Cy) bonds, respectively. O¨ nneby et al. reported that a fresh SiC surface is characterized by a main peak at 100.1 eV while a second peak at 101.8 eV appears when the SiC is exposed to the atmosphere for 20 min. This second peak was reported to reach a maximum intensity after 2 days exposure to air. Subsequent exposure resulted in the second peak decreasing in intensity accompanied by the emergence of a third peak at 102.5 eV, attributed to the transformation of the SiOx–Cy to SiO2. Thus, for our study of WNxCy films deposited by ALD on SiC, substrate oxidation must be taken into consideration. In particular, given our previous studies of ALD WNxCy film growth on different SiO2 surfaces, oxidation of SiC to SiOx–Cy and/or SiO2 can be expected to influence WNxCy nucleation and growth. Selected TDS data shows masses 29 and 46 assigned to C2H5+ and C2H5–NH3+ fragments, respectively, released at 620°C. From the relatively high desorption temperature and thickness independent desorption intensity profile observed we conclude that these C2H5+ and C2H5–NH3+ fragments are generated from groups located near the substrate-film interface. Ethyl groups are also liberated from the bulk of the film, as evidenced by the ethyl signal at mass 29, intensity dependence on thickness. In support of this finding, energy filtered transmission electron microscopy (EFTEM) elemental maps show a 2 nm carbon-rich layer at the WNxCy–SiO2 interface. This 2 nm layer is probably formed from decomposition of the (C2H5)3B precursor. We propose that the initial reaction of the SiO2 substrate with TEB renders the surface carbon-rich and thus the film growth on SiO2 and SiC are similar.
